comment: The CLI the copilot is, and what it offers before it is asked. Shared because both processes need it: electron/ai.js decides what it will spawn, src/models.js decides what the dropdown shows, and two copies of that is how the two disagree. Same arrangement as vault-contract.json and zoom-steps.json. `command` is the binary spawned — one process per turn, with the vault as its working directory (cwd plus $PWD, since opencode v2 resolves its project from $PWD). There is no HTTP client here and no key of ours to keep: every model, and every gateway (OpenRouter, ZenMux, z.ai), is reached by configuring it inside opencode, where its key already lives. `fallbacks` is what the dropdown shows before the CLI has been asked — a seed, not a limit, because the catalogue is an account property this file cannot check a name against, so what the panel offers is what gets spawned. `offerByDefault` is true so a fresh install has something to answer with: with a single provider an empty default list left the model dropdown with nothing in it at all. `sources` names which upstream providers the catalogue keeps — the CLI reaches a dozen of them, the pane offers two — and a `freeOnly` source is trimmed to the models that cost nothing. `auth` is the argument list that answers whether the CLI is signed in. `grants` is what it can actually do in the read-only or write-capable provider mode, in the user's words: it takes no per-tool allowlist, so it is fenced only by that mode — the UI's Ask and Auto choices decide whether write access is confirmed first.

grants.read: read and search your notes, and fetch web pages
grants.propose: read and search your notes, propose edits for your review, and fetch web pages
grants.ask: read, edit and create notes, run shell commands inside the vault, and fetch web pages
grants.auto: read, edit and create notes, run shell commands anywhere on this Mac, and fetch web pages
